market_summary: US equity markets rallied on November 4-5, 2026 with the S&P 500, Nasdaq and Dow all posting strong gains amid a post-election rally, with mega-cap tech stocks (AAPL, MSFT, AMZN) showing buy signals and broader sentiment positive. Singapore's banking sector reported Q3 2026 results mid-week: DBS disappointed with 5% profit decline due to weak trading income, UOB beat on fee income but missed profit expectations with margin pressures ahead, while OCBC heads into results Friday after strong first-half performance. Regional factors include elevated geopolitical risks and higher energy prices weighing on bank earnings and economic outlooks.

items.headline: DBS Q3 2026 profit falls 5% YoY to S$2.81 billion, misses forecasts on trading income slump
items.summary: <cite index="3-3">Net profit fell 5% year-on-year to S$2.81 billion in the three months ended September, missing the Bloomberg estimate of S$2.96 billion</cite>. <cite index="2-4">Markets trading income plunged 65% to S$152 million from a year earlier and fell 68% sequentially amid unfavourable market conditions.</cite>

items.headline: DBS declares S$0.75 dividend per share for Q3 2026
items.summary: <cite index="2-7">DBS declared a total third-quarter dividend of 81 Singapore cents per share, comprising an ordinary dividend of 66 cents and a 15-cent capital return dividend</cite>.

items.headline: UOB Q3 2026 profit misses forecasts at S$1.25 billion despite record fee income; NIM guidance cut
items.summary: <cite index="22-3">UOB's net profit for the third quarter came in at SG$1.25 billion ($975.72 million), underperforming the mean estimate of SG$1.35 billion from two analysts</cite>. <cite index="22-5,22-6">UOB's CFO said NIM for the full year is likely to fall below 1.75 percent, down from the previous quarter's guidance of 1.75 percent to 1.80 percent. For the third quarter, the bank's NIM narrowed 6 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 1.68 percent due to higher funding costs.</cite>

items.headline: UOB records record Q3 fee income of S$733 million, up 19% YoY
items.summary: <cite index="20-4,20-5">Net fee income in the third quarter hit a record S$733mil, a 19% increase from the same period a year ago. It also marked a 10% increase over the previous quarter.</cite>

items.headline: OCBC Q3 2026 results due Friday, Nov 6 after strong first-half performance
items.summary: <cite index="14-8">OCBC entered Q3 on the back of its strongest-ever first half: S$4.19 billion net profit for 1H 2026, a 13% year-on-year improvement.</cite> OCBC Q3 results are scheduled for release before market open on Friday, November 6.

items.headline: Dow Jones futures rise after Apple, Microsoft, Amazon flash buy signals in post-election rally
items.summary: Tech mega-caps AAPL, MSFT and AMZN showed strong buy signals amid a broad market rally following the US elections on November 4-5, 2026, driving futures higher.

items.headline: Apple CEO cites 'unprecedented' memory prices, suggests cost pressures on iPhone, Mac, iPad
items.summary: Apple CEO warned that memory prices are 'unprecedented' and could keep climbing, potentially putting fresh pressure on device costs including iPhones, Macs and iPads.

items.headline: Analyst resets Nvidia stock target after Intel crash
items.summary: A 5-star analyst reset Nvidia's stock price target following Intel's recent difficulties in the semiconductor sector.

items.headline: AMD hit with S1.1 billion charge related to Meta and OpenAI deals
items.summary: AMD incurred a S1.1 billion charge related to its dealings with Meta and OpenAI, impacting the semiconductor company's financials.

items.headline: Google turns off AI for schoolchildren by default
items.summary: Google has disabled its AI features by default for child users, signaling a shift in privacy and safety policies for younger audiences.

items.headline: Amazon workers in Greater Toronto Area launch unionization campaign with Unifor
items.summary: Amazon warehouse workers in the Greater Toronto Area have launched a unionization effort in partnership with Unifor, seeking better jobs and conditions.
